non_blocking_findings.title: qualified_but_unselected mixes CPU oracle qualification with native selected qualification
non_blocking_findings.evidence: coverage/any() comes from recomputed float32 CPU IoU (primary), while selected failure comes from the saved native GPU IoU. The field is emitted as qualified_but_unselected at line 157. Lines 134-135 already recognize that these predicates may differ.
non_blocking_findings.consequence: When CPU selected IoU passes a threshold and its saved native IoU does not, this formula can count that selected query as evidence of an unselected qualifying candidate. The reverse disagreement can hide a CPU selection failure. Native primary hit counts, repairs/damages, and the transfer are unaffected.
non_blocking_findings.minimal_correction: Report native unselected coverage from the saved native full256 oracle label together with the saved native selected IoU. Separately report CPU unselected coverage using primary.any(...) together with chosen. Keep the existing CPU/native threshold and oracle mismatch counts. Do not add a tolerance, fallback, or rerun.
non_blocking_findings.limitation: No actual completed artifacts were examined; this is a source-level inconsistency, not a claim that this run exhibits a threshold flip.
non_blocking_findings.disposition: Non-blocking for collection and native metric recount; correct the diagnostic before using it to claim a selection bottleneck.
